✉️
Congratulatory Message from Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
Sergey Lavrov
to Executive Secretary of the Preparatory Commission for the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization
Robert Floyd
(24 September 2026)
✍️
Dear Dr. Floyd,
Please, accept my sincere congratulations on
the 30th anniversary of the opening for signature of the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
.
☝️
Thirty years ago, a fundamentally important step was taken, reflecting the aspiration of the international community to establish a reliable barrier against the proliferation and modernization of the nuclear weapons.
The Treaty became a tangible expression of
the collective responsibility
of States for preserving global stability and security for future generations.
Its significance can hardly be overestimated: prohibition of nuclear tests is not merely an arms control measure, but also a powerful political signal on priority of peaceful development and dialogue in international affairs. The principles enshrined in the CTBT
remain valid for today as well
.
I highly appreciate the efforts that You and Your colleagues are undertaking for universalization of the Treaty. Your work represents
a daily contribution for maintaining trust among States
and creating conditions for preserving the international architecture of arms control and nuclear nonproliferation, and a clear example of how professionalism, dedication to the cause and concerted efforts can ensure the relevance of the most important international agreements even in challenging political circumstances.
The Russian Federation has consistently
regarded the CTBT as one of the key elements of the international security architecture
and advocates for CTBT's early entry into force. Achieving this objective requires the consolidation of efforts by all States, firm political will and readiness to place common interests above biased considerations. We stand ready to contribute to the achievement of this goal.
🤝
On this momentous occasion, I wish You and all staff members of the Provisional Technical Secretariat of the Preparatory Commission for the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization every success in Your highly responsible work for the sake of international peace and security.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates of Jordan Ayman Safadi
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇯🇴 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates of Jordan Ayman Safadi held a meeting in New York on the sidelines of the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly . The discussion focused on priority tasks for further strengthening traditionally friendly Russia-Jordan relations . Particular attention was paid to the outcomes of the 7th meeting of the Russia-Jordan Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation , held in Moscow on September 9-10. The Sides exchanged views on key Middle Eastern issues, focusing on the consequences of the unprecedented military escalation in the region in the context of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran . They also discussed the situation in the Palestinian-Israeli conflict zone . #RussiaJordan

🏔
September 24 – a memorable date in Russia’s military history.
2️⃣
2️⃣
7️⃣
years ago,
Russian troops under legendary commander Alexander Suvorov
stormed the St Gotthard Pass
, opening one of the most heroic chapters of his
Swiss campaign
.
In 1799, following brilliant victories in Italy,
Suvorov’s army was ordered to cross the Alps
and join
Alexander Rimsky-Korsakov
’s corps as well as Austrian allies in Switzerland. The commander chose
the shortest yet exceptionally difficult route
– through mountain passes held by French troops.
⚔️
On September 24, speed, resolve and flanking manoeuvres
enabled the Russian soldiers to overcome enemy resistance at St Gotthard. The very next day, they had to fight their way through the narrow Urnerloch rock tunnel and seize
the Devil’s Bridge
, suspended above the raging waters of the River Reuss. It seemed an impossible feat.
The French
demolished part of the bridge
, hoping to halt the advance. Yet, under fire, Russian soldiers
repaired the bridge
(!), lashing planks together with officers’ sashes, and pressed on with their attack, combining devastating close-range musket volleys with bayonet charges.
🪶
In his report to Emperor
Paul I
, Suvorov
wrote
:
“The troops of Your Imperial Majesty passed through a dark mountain cave and seized the bridge, miraculously formed by nature between two mountains and named "Teufelsbrücke". The enemy had destroyed it, but this did not stop the victors. The planks were tied together with officers' sashes, and across these planks they ran, descending from the heights, reaching the enemy and striking them from every direction...”
Further battles and severe hardships
lay ahead
: steep mountain trails, snow, bitter cold and a shortage of food.
News of the defeat of Rimsky-Korsakov’s corps changed the entire campaign plan: Suvorov now had to lead his army out of encirclement.
By October 7, 1799, he had accomplished this task: crossing snow-covered Alpine passes, the Russian army broke through enemy lines, retaining its fighting strength.
🎖
For
the Swiss campaign
, which exemplified the resilience of Russian soldiers and Suvorov’s mastery as a commander, Emperor Paul I awarded him the highest military rank –
Generalissimo
.
***
🇨🇭
To this day, the Swiss people remember the heroism of the Russian soldiers who fought against the French occupiers.
In 1898, a
12-metre memorial cross
, carved into the mountain and funded by Prince Sergey Golitsyn, was unveiled near the Devil’s Bridge. In 1999, a
monument to Suvorov
was erected at the St Gotthard Pass to mark the campaign’s bicentenary.
Every year,
Russian compatriots gather at the monument
, joined by friends from Switzerland and neighbouring countries,
to honour the memory of the Russian soldiers and pay tribute to the great commander
.

item.title: ⚡️ #KievRegimeCrimes Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: #KievRegimeCrimes ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : ❗️ Governor of Russia's Kursk Region Alexander Khinshtein has shared photographic evidence of another Ukrainian war crime – the destruction of St George’s Church, a historical and cultural heritage site in the Rylsk district. According to Alexander Khinshtein , the church stood in the village of Kozino, one kilometre from the state border. The wooden church was built in 1844, but its history goes back much further: the earliest mention dates to 1648, in a tax record. In 1662, the chapel was ravaged. In 1699, it received a new antimension and was consecrated. Over the centuries, the church on this site has perished and risen again more than once. The hundreds of crimes already committed by the Kiev regime against historical and religious sites make clear that the Zelensky regime has chosen to wage war on history and the faith of its forebears.
